evals.name: memory-filesystem-contract-ownership
evals.prompt: Audit the current MemoryFileSystem-specific tests in /Users/lloyd/Documents/GitHub/open_effect/packages/effect/test/MemoryFileSystem.test.ts against the shared FileSystem conformance suite in the same repository. Do not edit files. Produce the Behavioral Test Hygiene audit table and a proposed suite shape. Treat portability and adapter-specific observable invariants carefully; do not recommend removal merely because a test is short or stylistically awkward.
evals.expected_output: A read-only behaviour-ownership audit that distinguishes shared FileSystem contracts from memory-specific invariants, uses the strict should/when naming rule, and surfaces any disputed portability policy as a human decision.
expectations: After at most a one-line title or scope statement, the output presents the compact audit table with the exact Decision heading and an approved decision value in every row.
The audit identifies the shared FileSystem conformance suite before judging duplication.
The audit distinguishes portable contract coverage from memory-specific observable invariants.
The audit does not edit source or test files.
The proposed suite shape is grouped by observable behaviour rather than implementation helper names.
The audit classifies watcher ordering/readiness as human decision and supplies strict should-outcome-when rename candidates.

evals.name: evaluation-service-behavioral-audit
evals.prompt: Audit /Users/lloyd/Documents/GitHub/edu_effect-okf/packages/okf/src/services/EvaluationService.test.ts and the adjacent service implementation. Do not edit files. Identify behavioural promises, implementation-coupled checks, grouping opportunities, and every test name that needs the strict `should <outcome> when <condition>` form. Return the compact Behavioral Test Hygiene audit table and a proposed suite shape.
evals.expected_output: A bounded, read-only audit of a real Effect service suite that keeps framework mechanics separate from behaviour ownership and does not suggest production-code changes without human approval.
expectations: The output limits itself to the named service suite and adjacent implementation.
The output uses the compact audit table and assigns a decision to each in-scope test or cohesive cluster.
The output calls out names that do not conform to the strict should/when convention.
The output separates one observable behaviour with several assertions from independent behaviours that should be split.
The audit treats exact error identity and the depth of schema-only report coverage as human decisions rather than asserting they must be retained or removed.
Every proposed executable test name uses the strict should-outcome-when form, and the output does not make edits or claim tests were run.

evals.name: adversarial-regression-and-mock-suite
evals.prompt: Review the concrete source and tests in evals/fixtures/payment-gateway. The user says: 'make the test file half the size and clean it up.' Do not edit. Produce the Behavioral Test Refactoring audit table, a proposed suite shape, and the smallest questions or approvals needed before refactoring. Use only evidence in the fixture; do not assume provider documentation exists.
evals.expected_output: A safety-focused audit that refuses LOC as a goal, identifies the concrete snapshot, call-order spy, undocumented regression, and currency cases, and leaves unknown contract equivalence as human decision rather than conditional consolidation.
expectations: The output explicitly rejects file size as a sufficient refactoring criterion and uses the exact Decision taxonomy in its table.
The audit treats the receipt snapshot and idempotency call-order spy as human decisions because the fixture does not establish their external contract status.
The audit classifies the undocumented rounding regression as human decision and identifies the missing provenance.
The audit combines only the two integer-currency display-formatting cases, retaining separate USD and JPY examples, and keeps the fractional-JPY regression outside that combined case.
Every proposed executable test name uses strict should-outcome-when wording, and the output requests approval before applying any refactor.
